projected.source: Open-Meteo Climate API (CMIP6 HighResMIP models), daily temperature_2m_max

sentences.text: Days with an air temperature high of 90°F or more averaged 86.9 days a year in the 2000s and 111 days a year from 2016 to 2025.
The trend test found no clear trend yet for those days, so the record does not show a direction.
Climate models project about +24.0 more days a year at or above 90°F, with the models' change ranging from +14.4 to +50.6 days a year.
The models disagree on how large the change is, which is why a range is shown.
These are projections for a typical year in 2041 to 2050, on climate-model grids of about 20–50 km, downscaled by Open-Meteo to about 10 km, and are not a forecast of any single year or day.
Climate models are physics simulations that follow a high-emissions path, and the 26 years of past record are too few or too variable to tell a trend where none is reported.

past-air-hot-days.title: Days with an air temperature high of 90°F or more
past-air-hot-days.origin: Open-Meteo historical weather archive (ERA5 reanalysis), daily, 2000 to 2025. Counted from the daily record at this address.
past-air-hot-days.text: Days with an air temperature high of 90°F or more, 2000 to 2025. 2000s: 86.9 days a year on average (869 days in 10 years); 2016 to 2025 (the last 10 years): 111 days a year on average (1110 days in 10 years). Trend test (Mann-Kendall with Sen slope, one value per year; a trend counts only if p is under 0.05). Result: no clear trend yet.

future-hot-days.title: Days per year with an air-temperature high of 90°F or more, in climate models
future-hot-days.origin: Open-Meteo Climate API (CMIP6 HighResMIP models), daily temperature_2m_max. 7 of 7 CMIP6 HighResMIP models had data for this point.
future-hot-days.text: The climate models' own change in days a year at or above 90°F (air temperature, not feels-like), 7 models. Climate models: 113.5/yr (2001 to 2020, models) to 137.5/yr (2041 to 2050), about +24.0 days a year. Across models the change ranges from +14.4 to +50.6 days a year. Models range from 108.7 to 123.1 in 2001 to 2020 and from 127.7 to 164.1 in 2041 to 2050.

caveat.title: What the projections are, and are not
caveat.origin: Open-Meteo Climate API; CMIP6 HighResMIP climate models
caveat.text: Climate models (CMIP6) are physics simulations, not a forecast, so we show their change. These models follow a high-emissions path (as close to RCP8.5 as CMIP6 gets). We show how much they say it changes, not their raw level. The models run on climate-model grids of about 20–50 km, downscaled by Open-Meteo to about 10 km, and they disagree, so the range across models is shown. They describe how often hot days could occur in a typical year of 2041 to 2050, not what any single year or day will do. A trend in the past record is reported only when a statistical test gives p under 0.05; otherwise the record says "no clear trend yet", which means the 26 years are too few or too variable to tell.
